q: A job is costed on the basis of the gang actually employed on it. If more men are deployed on the job than the standard gang composition for such work, the usual effect on the cost of the job is that:

options.A: Labour cost rises without a proportionate increase in outturn, making the job costlier
options.B: Labour cost falls automatically
options.C: There is no effect on the cost of the job
options.D: Material cost of the job rises instead

q: Under a group incentive arrangement, the group leader's role in relation to the group's outturn is mainly to:

options.A: Fix the allowed times for the group's jobs
options.B: Organise and distribute the work within the group, and ensure that material, tools and drawings are available so that the group maintains its outturn
options.C: Compile the cost of the group's jobs in the accounts office
options.D: Inspect and pass the outturn of his own group finally

q: On a day, a worker's gate card shows full attendance, but the time shown on his job cards accounts for only part of the day, with no idle time card or leave record for the balance. The correct course for the workshop accounts office is to:

options.A: Charge the unexplained balance automatically to the first job card
options.B: Ignore the difference, since the gate card alone governs payment
options.C: Treat the whole day as idle time without enquiry
options.D: Have the discrepancy enquired into and the unaccounted time properly explained and booked before the labour cost is finalised

q: Time lost by a worker in arriving late at the workshop is treated in workshop time booking as:

options.A: Time worked on the job he was to start
options.B: Idle time chargeable to shop on-cost as a matter of course
options.C: Time not worked, for which no job booking arises and which is dealt with as absence or loss of time for that period
options.D: Overtime earned by the worker

q: A job continues through more than one shift in a workshop working in shifts. The labour cost of the job is built up by:

options.A: Booking the time of the workers of each shift separately to the same work order, so that the total labour on the job covers all the shifts
options.B: Booking only the first shift's time, the later shifts being treated as on-cost
options.C: Opening a separate work order for every shift
options.D: Charging the night shift's time to general on-cost in all cases

q: A fitter of the machine shop is lent for a few days to the erecting shop, where he works on that shop's jobs. His time for those days should be booked:

options.A: To the jobs of his parent shop, since he belongs to it
options.B: As idle time of the machine shop
options.C: To the jobs of the erecting shop on which he actually worked
options.D: Half to each shop, irrespective of the work done

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Leave salary paid to shop staff for periods when they are on leave cannot be charged to any job.
2. Such leave salary is, therefore, borne as an overhead charge of the workshop.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

q: Material stored in a shop is destroyed by an accidental fire. In workshop costing, such a loss is treated as:

options.A: A normal part of the cost of the jobs in hand in the shop
options.B: An abnormal loss, to be reported and dealt with separately under proper sanction, and not absorbed silently in job costs
options.C: Shop on-cost of the following year
options.D: A reduction in the value of the outturn of the shop

q: Preventive maintenance of workshop machinery is carried out under prepared maintenance schedules mainly so that:

options.A: Machines are attended to at planned intervals during planned stoppages, instead of being allowed to break down in service
options.B: Maintenance staff remain employed throughout the year
options.C: The cost of maintenance can be charged to capital
options.D: Machines can be overhauled only after failure

q: The cost of breakdown maintenance of machines is recorded and watched machine-wise mainly in order to:

options.A: Fix the wages of the maintenance gang
options.B: Bring out machines whose repeated breakdown repairs are becoming costly, for decisions on major repair or replacement
options.C: Work out the incentive bonus of the operators
options.D: Price the articles produced on the machines directly

q: A periodical analysis of rejected work in a workshop, classifying rejections by shop and by cause, is undertaken mainly to:

options.A: Decide the punishment of individual workers in every case
options.B: Value the rejected articles for stock purposes
options.C: Fix the sale price of scrap
options.D: Identify the recurring causes of rejection so that corrective action can reduce defective work and its cost

q: The cost of poor quality in a workshop comprises, besides the value of rejected material, such hidden elements as:

options.A: The price realised from the sale of scrap
options.B: The wages of the inspection staff on regular establishment only
options.C: The cost of rework and rectification, re-inspection of rectified work and the outturn lost while defects are attended to
options.D: The bonus earned on accepted outturn

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure on safety measures in a workshop, such as machine guards and safety training of staff, serves the workshop generally and is not identifiable with individual jobs.
2. Such expenditure is accordingly borne as an overhead charge of the workshop.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: At the monthly review of a workshop's working, the actual outturn is compared with the target or programme for the month mainly so that:

options.A: Shortfalls can be identified in time and the programme, priorities and resources of the following periods adjusted
options.B: The work orders of the month can all be closed
options.C: The on-cost percentages for the next year can be sanctioned
options.D: The incentive bonus rates can be revised at once

q: The cost per unit of Periodic Overhaul of a class of stock has been rising steadily over successive periods, though the scope of overhaul is unchanged. For the workshop accounts office, this trend is principally a signal to:

options.A: Raise the on-cost percentage at once
options.B: Analyse the labour, material and on-cost elements of the unit cost to locate where the increase is arising
options.C: Stop the overhaul of that class of stock
options.D: Transfer the stock to another workshop without enquiry

q: For work done by a workshop for a private party, the recovery of the cost is ensured in the workshop accounts office by:

options.A: Leaving the recovery to the shop which executed the work
options.B: Charging the cost to shop on-cost after completion
options.C: Raising a bill for the amount due and watching its realisation till the amount is recovered
options.D: Adjusting the cost against the wages of the staff employed

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Outstanding work orders under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense are reviewed periodically by the workshop accounts office with the executive.
2. The object of the review is to get completed jobs transferred out and old or infructuous balances cleared, so that the suspense does not accumulate.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: When a workshop is closed or reorganised and its work is transferred to another unit, the balances relating to jobs in progress, materials and other workshop assets are dealt with by:

options.A: Writing them off automatically on the date of closure
options.B: Leaving them permanently in the books of the closed workshop
options.C: Charging them to the revenue of the year of closure in all cases
options.D: Transferring them to the receiving unit through proper transfer entries, so that the receiving unit takes over the work with its accumulated cost

q: The workshop accounts office keeps the workshop executive informed of the progressive outlay against the budget allotment of the workshop mainly so that:

options.A: Expenditure can be regulated within the allotment and excess over it avoided or regularised in time
options.B: The allotment can be surrendered at the start of the year
options.C: Work orders can be opened without sanctioned estimates
options.D: The outturn statement can be dispensed with

q: A development job, undertaken to develop an improved component or method for future use, is costed in a workshop by:

options.A: Merging its cost in the cost of the regular production jobs of the shop
options.B: Executing it under a distinct work order so that the cost of the development effort is ascertained and watched separately
options.C: Charging it to the wages account of the staff engaged on it
options.D: Treating it as scrap work of the shop

q: Work of an experimental nature, whose results are yet to be proved, is executed in a workshop under:

options.A: The standing work order for routine repairs
options.B: The work order of any regular manufacture job in progress
options.C: General on-cost, without any work order
options.D: A separate experimental work order, so that its cost and results can be evaluated before the work is adopted regularly

q: A manufactured article supplied by the workshop develops a defect within its guarantee period and is returned for attention. The cost of putting the defect right is borne as:

options.A: A fresh charge on the user, as if it were a new job
options.B: Shop on-cost of an unrelated shop
options.C: A charge on the stores depot which stocked the article
options.D: A cost of the manufacturing workshop, the article having been guaranteed by it, and not as a fresh revenue job of the user

q: The time spent by a machinist in setting up his machine for a particular batch of components is treated in costing as:

options.A: Idle time of the machine shop
options.B: Time booked to the batch or job for which the setting was made, forming part of its labour cost
options.C: General on-cost of the workshop as a whole in all cases
options.D: Leave time of the machinist

q: The cost of the drawing and design office of a workshop, which prepares drawings for the work of the workshop generally, is treated as:

options.A: A direct charge on the first job for which a drawing is made each month
options.B: Proforma on-cost of the workshop
options.C: A charge on the stores depot attached to the workshop
options.D: General on-cost, since the office serves the workshop as a whole

q: A workshop introduces a second shift on its existing machines, and the outturn increases while the fixed general overheads of the workshop remain broadly the same. The usual effect on costing is that:

options.A: The general on-cost is spread over a larger outturn, so that the on-cost burden per unit of outturn tends to fall
options.B: The general on-cost per unit rises in the same proportion as the outturn
options.C: General on-cost ceases to be charged altogether
options.D: Direct labour cost per unit necessarily doubles

q: The agreement between the job costs compiled in the Workshop General Register and the corresponding control figures in the financial books is checked in order to ensure that:

options.A: The incentive bonus has been calculated correctly
options.B: The cost accounts and the financial accounts of the workshop tally with each other and neither has omitted or duplicated a booking
options.C: The outturn programme of the workshop is fulfilled
options.D: The stores balances of the depot agree with the stock sheets

q: Where the maintenance of a workshop machine is entrusted to an outside agency under a maintenance contract, the payments made under the contract are booked in the same manner as the cost of:

options.A: A manufacture job for the stores depot
options.B: Repairs and maintenance of the machine concerned, under the appropriate standing arrangement for machinery repairs
options.C: New machinery under the Machinery and Plant Programme
options.D: Incentive bonus of the maintenance staff

q: The cost of internal transport facilities of a workshop, such as cranes and tractors which move material between shops, is brought into workshop costing by treating such facilities as:

options.A: Direct labour of the jobs moved
options.B: Capital assets written off in the year of purchase
options.C: A charge on the railway's traffic earnings
options.D: A service facility whose cost is borne in the on-cost of the shops served

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. When the method of working or the machine used for an operation is changed, the allowed time for that operation requires revision.
2. Continuing with the old allowed time after such a change would distort the time saved and the bonus earned on the operation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Rolling stock is admitted into a workshop for Periodic Overhaul:

options.A: Whenever it arrives at the workshop gate, irrespective of the programme
options.B: Only against the overhaul programme and the capacity of the workshop, so that stock is not detained in the shop without work and the programme is maintained
options.C: Only after the stock has failed in service
options.D: At the discretion of the stores depot holding its material

q: An outline process chart prepared in method study of a workshop job records:

options.A: Every transportation, delay and storage in full detail
options.B: Only the main activities of the process, namely the operations and inspections, omitting the subsidiary movements and delays
options.C: The wages payable for each operation of the job
options.D: The simultaneous movements of the two hands of the operator

q: A flow diagram used in method study in a workshop is:

options.A: A chart of the wages distributed over the jobs of a shop
options.B: A statement of the material flowing from the depot to the shops
options.C: A register of the jobs in progress in a shop
options.D: A scale plan of the work area on which the paths of movement of men or material are drawn, so that wasteful movement can be spotted and reduced

q: In method study, after the existing method has been critically examined, the improved method is developed by applying the approach of:

options.A: Eliminating unnecessary work, combining operations where possible, rearranging their sequence and simplifying the remaining work
options.B: Increasing the gang strength on every operation of the job
options.C: Revising the allowed times before changing the method of working
options.D: Transferring the job to another shop of the workshop

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Allocation of overheads means charging the whole of an overhead item directly to the one cost centre which alone incurred it.
2. Apportionment of overheads means distributing a common overhead item over the cost centres benefiting from it on an equitable basis.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the primary distribution of workshop overheads, the overheads are apportioned to all cost centres of the workshop, production and service centres alike.
2. In the secondary distribution, the cost collected at service centres is charged directly to individual jobs, without passing through the production shops served.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: In process costing in a workshop, the partly finished units lying in a process at the close of a period are expressed in terms of completed units for costing purposes. This measure is known as:

options.A: Standard hours
options.B: Scrap value
options.C: Equivalent production
options.D: Conversion cost

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Loss of material inherent in a process, within the limit expected for that process, is treated as normal loss and its cost is borne by the good output of the process.
2. Loss beyond the expected limit is treated as abnormal loss, is excluded from the process cost and is dealt with separately.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A fitting shop does work predominantly by hand, machine work being negligible, but its on-cost is absorbed on jobs on a machine-hour basis. The likely result is that:

options.A: The cost of every job of the shop becomes more accurate than before
options.B: Jobs are charged with on-cost on a basis unrelated to the way the shop's expenses arise, so that job costs are distorted
options.C: The on-cost of the shop is over-absorbed in every period as a rule
options.D: The labour cost of the jobs of the shop disappears from the cost sheets

q: Material issued for a specific manufacture job is wrongly booked in the on-cost folio of the shop instead of to the work order of the job. Until the booking is corrected, the position is that:

options.A: The total cost of the workshop as a whole is increased by the error
options.B: The stores depot remains out of pocket for the material issued
options.C: The wages payable to the workers of the shop are reduced
options.D: The job is under-costed and the on-cost of the shop is overstated, so that other jobs of the shop bear a burden not belonging to them

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Work done for an outside body on a deposit-work basis is secured by a deposit of the estimated cost, together with the charges leviable, taken from the party in advance.
2. Work done for another railway is settled between the two railways through transfer transactions, and no deposit is taken from the other railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Serviceable material drawn for a job and returned to the stores depot as surplus is credited to the job at its stock (issue) value.
2. Scrap arising on a job is credited to the job at the value realised or assessed for the scrap, and not at the original issue value of the material from which it arose.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Job costing suits a non-repetitive order executed to a specific requirement, the cost being collected for that order as a whole.
2. Batch costing suits standard components manufactured in lots for stocking, the cost being collected for the lot as a whole.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Estimated costing is used to work out in advance the expected cost of a one-off job, as when a quotation is to be given for outside work.
2. Standard costing suits repetitive manufacture, where standard costs are prescribed beforehand and the actual cost is compared with them.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the CLW pattern incentive scheme, the worker is paid on the full allowed time of the accepted work done by him, so that he receives the whole value of the time saved by him.
2. Under the Halsey premium plan, the worker receives only a share of the value of the time saved by him, the rest of the saving going to the employer.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Neither 1 nor 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Both 1 and 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The works cost of a workshop job is built up by adding the shop on-cost absorbed on it to its prime cost.
2. The full cost of the job is arrived at by adding the general on-cost and the proforma on-cost to the works cost, so that the cost of the outturn becomes comparable with trade prices.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Manufacture of articles for stocking in the stores depot is taken in hand against the demand or indent of the depot, and not at the discretion of the shop.
2. Manufacture for stock in excess of the depot's requirement locks up funds in stock which may in time become surplus in the depot.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In production control, routing and scheduling of a job precede its dispatching to the shops, and follow-up of the job comes after it has been so released.
2. In production control, dispatching of a job precedes its routing, the path of the job through the shops being decided only after work has begun in the first shop.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: 1 only

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The job card of a worker records the time spent by him on a job.
2. The piece-work ticket records the quantity produced by the worker and passed on inspection, on the basis of which payment by results is made to him.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A snap gauge is used in a workshop for:

options.A: Quickly checking whether an external dimension of a turned component lies within its prescribed limits
options.B: Measuring the depth of a blind hole in a component
options.C: Checking the pitch of a screw thread
options.D: Marking out work on a casting before machining

q: In a foundry mould, the sprue is the passage through which:

options.A: Air and gases generated in the mould escape to the outside
options.B: The core of the casting is supported in its position
options.C: Molten metal is poured down into the mould cavity through the gating system
options.D: Excess molten metal rises up to show that the mould is full

q: Spot facing of a drilled hole in a component is carried out in order to:

options.A: Cut a conical recess for the head of a countersunk screw
options.B: Provide a flat, level seat around the hole for the head of a bolt or for a nut
options.C: Enlarge the hole to a larger diameter throughout its length
options.D: Finish the surface of the hole to a fine accuracy

q: Chamfering of the end of a shaft or of the edge of a component in a workshop means:

options.A: Cutting a groove around the circumference of the shaft
options.B: Producing a roughened surface on the shaft for a better grip
options.C: Cutting a screw thread on the end of the shaft
options.D: Bevelling the sharp edge, so that assembly with the mating part is eased and the sharp corner is removed

q: Tack welding is resorted to in the fabrication of a structure in a workshop in order to:

options.A: Hold the parts in correct alignment by means of small temporary welds before the final welding is carried out
options.B: Test the strength of the finished weld of the structure
options.C: Cut the plates of the structure to the sizes required
options.D: Harden the surface of the welded joint

q: Facing sand is used in a foundry mould for:

options.A: Filling the bulk of the mould behind the face of the pattern
options.B: Making the cores required for the casting
options.C: Forming the layer of sand in contact with the pattern, so that the casting gets a smooth surface finish
options.D: Lining the cupola furnace of the foundry

q: Under the hole-basis system of limits and fits followed in workshop manufacture:

options.A: The shaft is kept at a standard size and the hole is varied to obtain the fit required
options.B: The hole is kept at a standard (basic) size and the shaft is varied to obtain the fit required
options.C: Both the hole and the shaft are varied for every fit
options.D: No allowance is provided between the mating parts in any fit

q: Inspection of workshop outturn is kept organisationally separate from the shop which produced the article mainly so that:

options.A: The cost of inspection can be charged directly to the article inspected
options.B: The producing shop is relieved of keeping its production records
options.C: Rejected articles can be disposed of by the inspection staff without record
options.D: Acceptance or rejection of the outturn is decided impartially, the producing shop not being left to pass its own work

q: A standard cost card prescribed for a component manufactured repetitively in a workshop sets out:

options.A: The standard quantities of material, the standard labour time for each operation and the on-cost to be charged for the component, against which its actual cost of production is compared
options.B: The names of the workers who will be engaged on the component
options.C: The price at which the component is sold in the open market
options.D: The production programme of the shop for the following year

q: The cost sheet of a workshop job differs from the folio of the job in the Workshop General Register in that the cost sheet:

options.A: Is maintained by the shop and not by the Workshop Accounts Office
options.B: Records only the material cost of the job
options.C: Is a summary of the final cost of the completed job drawn from the register folio, whereas the folio is the running record in which labour, material and on-cost are posted as the job progresses
options.D: Is prepared before the job is taken in hand in the shop

q: A machine which has been surveyed and condemned as beyond economical repair is finally dealt with by:

options.A: Retaining it in the Plant Register indefinitely at its full book value
options.B: Striking it off the Plant Register under competent sanction and disposing of the released material through the stores depot as scrap
options.C: Transferring its book value to the work order in progress in the shop
options.D: Charging its book value to the shop on-cost of the year of condemnation

q: Drawals of material on a manufacture job are checked in the workshop with reference to the bill of materials (material schedule) of the job mainly in order to ensure that:

options.A: The stores depot issues the material at the lowest available price
options.B: The job is completed before its programme date
options.C: The allowed time fixed for the job is not exceeded
options.D: Material is not drawn in excess of the scheduled requirement of the job, and excess drawal, if any, is brought to notice and accounted for

q: On completion of the Periodic Overhaul of a unit of rolling stock in a workshop, the unit is returned to service:

options.A: Only after it has been inspected and certified as fit to run, the overhaul being complete in all respects
options.B: As soon as the shop reports the work as finished, without any inspection
options.C: Only after the cost of its overhaul has been paid in cash by the operating department
options.D: After it has been repainted, whether or not its mechanical overhaul is complete

q: Material held in the stores depot attached to a workshop remains in the custody and accountal of the stores depot until:

options.A: The close of the financial year
options.B: The workshop completes its annual outturn programme
options.C: It is actually issued to a shop against a requisition for a work order
options.D: The Workshop Accounts Officer orders its transfer to the shops generally

q: Work done by a workshop for its own railway is cleared out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense on completion by a transfer entry to the final head concerned, and not against a cash payment, because:

options.A: The cost of such work is never ascertained in the workshop
options.B: The workshop and the indenting department both belong to the same railway, so that the transaction is settled by book adjustment within the accounts of that railway
options.C: The stores depot pays in cash for all work done for the railway
options.D: All revenue work of a workshop is written off at the close of the year

q: The cost of maintaining the standards (gauge) room of a workshop, which checks and calibrates the gauges and measuring instruments of all the shops, is borne in workshop costing as:

options.A: A direct charge on the job under manufacture at the time
options.B: Proforma on-cost of the workshop
options.C: A charge on the stores depot attached to the workshop
options.D: General on-cost, since the room serves the workshop as a whole

q: After manufacture or heavy repair in the boiler shop, a boiler is subjected to a hydraulic (hydrostatic) test mainly in order to:

options.A: Prove the soundness and tightness of its plates and joints under pressure before it is put into service
options.B: Remove the scale formed on its internal surfaces
options.C: Ascertain the weight of the boiler for its records
options.D: Prepare its outer surface for painting

q: The overhaul capacity of the erecting shop of a repair workshop is governed mainly by:

options.A: The number of clerks posted in the shop office
options.B: The value of the material held in the stores depot
options.C: The number of berths or pits available on which stock can be placed for overhaul, together with the gangs that can be deployed on them
options.D: The number of work orders opened in the workshop in the year

q: Machines in a workshop are lubricated according to a prepared lubrication schedule mainly in order to:

options.A: Charge the cost of lubricating oil directly to individual jobs
options.B: Reduce friction and wear of the moving parts and keep the machines in efficient working condition
options.C: Keep the lubrication staff employed on every shift
options.D: Increase the standing charges of the machines

q: Surplus material returned by a shop to the stores depot is credited to the work order of the job:

options.A: As soon as the shop reports that the material has become surplus
options.B: At the close of the financial year in all cases
options.C: Without any acknowledgement of receipt from the depot
options.D: On the depot acknowledging receipt of the material under a return note, so that the credit is supported by the depot's accountal of the material received back

q: Marking out (layout) of a workpiece in the fitting shop, before it is machined or fabricated, consists of:

options.A: Scribing on the workpiece, from its drawing, the lines and centres to which it is to be worked
options.B: Painting the workpiece all over to prevent it from rusting
options.C: Weighing the workpiece before it is sent to the machine
options.D: Testing the hardness of the workpiece at several points

q: During internal check, the Workshop Accounts Office finds that a shop has incurred expenditure on a job for which no work order has been received in the accounts office. The correct course is to:

options.A: Book the expenditure to shop on-cost and proceed with the payment
options.B: Admit the bills for payment and regularise the matter at the close of the year
options.C: Hold the booking, bring the matter to notice and have a proper work order issued under the sanctioned estimate before the expenditure is admitted in the accounts
options.D: Charge the expenditure to the first open work order of the shop

q: A workshop has overhauled rolling stock belonging to another railway, but the bill raised against that railway covers only the material and labour booked on the job, the on-cost and proforma charges having been omitted. The consequence of the omission is that:

options.A: The home railway gains financially by the omission
options.B: The cost of the overhaul is under-recovered from the owning railway, and the home railway bears a part of the cost of work done for the other railway
options.C: The overhaul becomes chargeable to the revenue overhaul head of the home railway
options.D: The bill must be cancelled and the work treated as the home railway's own overhaul work

q: The unit cost of the same class of overhaul differs widely between two workshops, and it is found that the two workshops follow different bases for absorbing on-cost on jobs. In these circumstances, comparison of the costs of the two workshops is meaningful only if:

options.A: Both workshops employ the same number of staff
options.B: The stock overhauled in both workshops is of the same age
options.C: Both workshops surrender their unspent budget allotment
options.D: Both workshops compile their costs on uniform costing principles and on comparable bases of on-cost absorption

q: On a repetitive job of a shop, the labour hours booked are persistently well in excess of the allowed time for the job, although the method of working and the machines used have not changed. For the Workshop Accounts Office, the proper course in the matter is to:

options.A: Bring the persistent excess to the notice of the executive and the work study organisation for investigation of its cause, instead of merely passing the cost period after period
options.B: Reduce the wages of the workers engaged on the job forthwith
options.C: Transfer the excess hours to shop on-cost without any enquiry
options.D: Close the work order of the job and open a fresh work order in its place

q: A worker who holds tools on loan from his shop is transferred out of the workshop. Before he is relieved from the workshop, his tool account should be:

options.A: Transferred as it stands to the worker who joins in his place, without any check
options.B: Written off in full as a consumable charge of the shop
options.C: Cleared by his returning the tools issued to him, or accounting for any shortage under proper orders, so that no tool remains outstanding against him
options.D: Kept open until he retires from railway service

q: A workshop job has been completed and its outturn is ready for transfer, but the total cost booked on the job exceeds the amount of its sanctioned estimate. Before the outturn is transferred, the correct course is to:

options.A: Transfer the outturn at once, the excess over the estimate being ignored
options.B: Have the excess over the sanctioned estimate regularised by a revised or supplementary estimate sanctioned by the competent authority
options.C: Charge the amount of the excess to the shop on-cost of the shop
options.D: Recover the amount of the excess from the workers engaged on the job

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Semi-variable overheads are partly fixed and partly variable in behaviour, changing with the volume of outturn but not in direct proportion to it.
2. The fixed element of a semi-variable overhead item disappears as soon as the outturn of the shop falls to nil.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A workshop starts an additional shift, and an extra chargeman has to be engaged for the supervision of that shift alone. The supervision cost of the shop rises at once by the whole of his pay, instead of rising gradually with the outturn. In terms of cost behaviour, this supervision cost is an example of:

options.A: A variable cost
options.B: A step cost
options.C: A direct cost of jobs
options.D: A sunk cost

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The power house of a workshop supplies power to the machine repair shop, and the repair shop maintains the plant of the power house, so that each of these service centres renders service to the other.
2. In the secondary distribution of overheads, the cost of such mutually serving service centres is reapportioned taking their services to each other into account, and not by ignoring the mutual service.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: In costing terminology, a by-product is:

options.A: The main product for which a process is carried on
options.B: Waste material of a process which has no realisable value
options.C: A defective article which is rectified and passed as good output
options.D: A secondary product of relatively small value which arises incidentally in the course of manufacturing the main product

q: Where two or more products, each of substantial value, are produced simultaneously from the same material and process, they are called joint products. The common cost incurred up to the point at which they become separately identifiable is known as:

options.A: The prime cost
options.B: The joint cost
options.C: The separable cost
options.D: The conversion cost

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the straight line method, the depreciation charged on an asset in each year remains the same throughout its life, being worked out on its original cost.
2. Under the written down value method, the depreciation charged decreases from year to year, as it is worked out on the diminishing book value of the asset.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A shop absorbs its on-cost on jobs as a percentage of the cost of material consumed on them. The price of its main material rises steeply, although the work done in the shop and the shop's own indirect expenses remain unchanged. The effect on the job costs of the shop will be that:

options.A: They become equal for all jobs, whatever material is used on them
options.B: They fall, because dearer material is used more economically by the shop
options.C: They remain unaffected, since the indirect expenses of the shop are unchanged
options.D: They rise, because the on-cost charged follows the inflated material cost instead of the activity of the shop

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Abnormal gain in a process arises when the actual loss in the process is less than the normal loss expected in that process.
2. The abnormal gain is valued at the cost per unit of the good output and is dealt with separately, and not by loading it on the normal cost working of the process.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a process (functional) layout, machines of the same type are grouped together in one shop or section, and a job is routed through the shops according to the operations it requires.
2. In a product (line) layout, the machines are arranged in the sequence of operations of one product, which suits repetitive manufacture of that product in quantity.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A large batch of standard bolts manufactured in a workshop is offered for inspection. Instead of examining every bolt, the inspector examines a sample drawn from the batch and accepts or rejects the whole batch on the result of the sample. This method of inspection is known as:

options.A: Stage inspection
options.B: First piece inspection
options.C: Patrol inspection
options.D: Acceptance sampling

q: Standardisation, as applied to the materials and components used in a workshop, means:

options.A: Confining them to a limited range of established sizes, types and specifications, instead of allowing an uncontrolled variety
options.B: Making every component of a special design suited to one job only
options.C: Purchasing all materials from one standard supplier only
options.D: Fixing one standard price for all materials in the stores depot

q: Job analysis, as carried out in an industrial organisation, consists of:

options.A: Determining the relative worth of a job for building the wage structure
options.B: Systematically collecting information about the duties, responsibilities and working conditions of a job
options.C: Assessing the efficiency and conduct of the worker holding a job
options.D: Timing a job with a stop watch to fix its allowed time

q: A two-handed process chart prepared in method study of a workshop operation records:

options.A: The work of a man and of the machine attended by him, side by side
options.B: The pattern of movement of men and materials in a work area
options.C: The sequence of operations, inspections and delays in a process
options.D: The movements of the two hands of an operator, recorded against a common time scale

q: A machine of a shop is given a major rebuild which substantially extends its useful life well beyond the life originally expected of it. The cost of such a rebuild is treated in workshop accounts as:

options.A: A charge recoverable from the operator of the machine
options.B: A part of the shop on-cost of the year in which the rebuild is done
options.C: A direct charge on the first job taken up on the machine after the rebuild
options.D: A capital or replacement charge, and not as an ordinary repair loaded on the shop on-cost

q: Taper turning on a centre lathe is the operation of producing:

options.A: A flat surface at the end of a workpiece
options.B: A grooved surface on a workpiece
options.C: A conical surface, uniformly tapering along the length of the workpiece
options.D: A screw thread on the workpiece

q: Grooving on a lathe consists of:

options.A: Cutting a narrow recess or channel around a turned surface
options.B: Producing a flat surface by a reciprocating tool
options.C: Enlarging a drilled hole to an accurate size
options.D: Impressing a diamond pattern on the surface of a handle

q: A three-jaw self-centring chuck of a lathe is so called because:

options.A: Its three jaws are adjusted one by one by hand
options.B: It can hold only square workpieces
options.C: It is used only for centring the tailstock of the lathe
options.D: Its three jaws move simultaneously together, so that round work held in it is centred automatically

q: A gear blank, whose bore has been finished, is mounted on a mandrel held between the centres of a lathe, and its outside is then turned. The blank is mounted on a mandrel for this work primarily so that:

options.A: The blank can be turned at a much higher speed than usual
options.B: No cutting tool is required for turning the outside
options.C: The turned outside surface is concentric with the finished bore of the blank
options.D: The bore of the blank is enlarged during the turning

q: Trepanning, as carried out on a plate in a workshop, is the operation of:

options.A: Cutting an annular groove with a rotating cutter, so that a large hole is produced leaving a solid core
options.B: Cutting a screw thread inside a hole
options.C: Smoothing a hole by means of an abrasive stone
options.D: Marking out the position of a hole on a plate

q: Shearing of sheet metal in a workshop is carried out by:

options.A: Melting the sheet along the line of cut with a gas flame
options.B: Two blades, one moving past the other, which cut the sheet between them, as in a guillotine shear
options.C: A rotating abrasive wheel run along the sheet
options.D: Hammering the sheet over a sharp edge until it separates

q: Riveting, as a method of joining plates in fabrication work, consists of:

options.A: Fusing the edges of the plates together by an electric arc
options.B: Joining the plates with bolts which can be removed at will
options.C: Coating the joint between the plates with solder
options.D: Joining the plates permanently by rivets passed through them, the ends of the rivets being formed into heads

q: Electroplating of a workshop article consists of:

options.A: Dipping the article in a bath of molten zinc
options.B: Spraying molten metal on the surface of the article
options.C: Depositing a thin layer of another metal on the article by passing an electric current through a suitable solution
options.D: Painting the article with metallic paint

q: In foundry practice, the gating system of a mould means:

options.A: The arrangement of cores placed inside the mould
options.B: The system of channels, comprising the sprue, the runners and the ingates, through which the molten metal flows into the mould cavity
options.C: The vents provided in the mould for the escape of gases
options.D: The flask in which the mould is made

q: Cracks are found in a casting which developed while it was cooling and contracting in the mould, at places where its contraction was hindered. Such cracks in a casting are known as:

options.A: Blow holes
options.B: Cold shuts
options.C: Hot tears
options.D: Scabs

q: In welding, an undercut at a joint means:

options.A: A groove melted into the parent metal at the toe or edge of the weld, reducing the thickness of the parent metal there
options.B: A layer of slag trapped inside the weld metal
options.C: A hole burnt right through the plates being welded
options.D: Excess weld metal deposited above the surface of the joint
